verdict: Coinbase swung to a $394M net loss as revenue fell 31% to $1.41B in a weak crypto market — a $482M paper loss on the crypto it holds as an investment did most of the damage, while the core business ran close to breakeven.

segments.name: Transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees from crypto trading — consumer $567M, institutional $136M, other $53M. Consumer volumes fell by more than half from a year ago; institutional grew after the Deribit acquisition.

segments.name: Subscription and services
segments.note: Steadier income: stablecoin revenue $305M, blockchain rewards $101M, interest and finance fees $68M, and other services $109M.

segments.note: Interest earned on Coinbase's own corporate cash — smaller as balances and rates fell.

follow100Note: Of every $100 Coinbase took in, $34.14 of the damage was paper losses on crypto it holds as an investment — non-cash marks that reverse if crypto prices recover. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Trading slowed with the market
takeaways.text: Transaction revenue fell 40% year over year to $756M as consumer trading volumes dropped 54%. Subscriptions and services fell only 14%, cushioning the downturn.

takeaways.title: Paper losses on Coinbase's own crypto
takeaways.text: The crypto Coinbase holds as an investment lost $482M on paper in the quarter — more than the entire $394M net loss. The core business ran close to breakeven, with an operating loss of just $21M.

takeaways.title: Cash covered the loss
takeaways.text: Coinbase ended the quarter with $10.2B of cash and equivalents, so the loss came out of a deep cushion — but it shows how quickly profits swing with crypto prices.

oneTimers: A $482M mark-to-market loss on crypto assets held for investment (versus a $597M loss a year ago) — non-cash, and it reverses if crypto prices rise.
Losses of $35M on crypto held for operations, also mark-to-market.
otherDetail: A $482M loss on crypto assets Coinbase holds as an investment, partly offset by $62M of other income (gains on other investments), less $23M of interest expense.
footerNote: Coinbase reports no gross-profit line; 'Transaction expense' — the direct cost of processing trades — is shown as cost of revenue. The quarter was a loss, so the slate 'Covered by cash on hand' block is the $394M net loss, funded from Coinbase's balance sheet. Figures are from Coinbase's Q1 2026 shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-Q.
